judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the Email address field of the Sign in form in the account tray (an off-canvas panel the account control opens; the snapshot places it at x=1310 in a 1280px viewport, but it is part of the page users receive and they fill it when they sign in). Its captured markup has type="email", a label, a placeholder and aria-describedby, but no autocomplete attribute, and the form has none either, so the claim is true of the capture. I looked for reasons it could pass: the field collects the user's own email address, a purpose in WCAG's Input Purposes list (email); type="email" only fixes the data format and does not say the address is the user's, and H98 (autocomplete) is the sufficient technique; the site's base, main and secondary scripts never set autocomplete on it (they only read its value for analytics), and the snapshot is the DOM after scripts. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same input without autocomplete, and the screenshot is a styled render, so the capture does not differ. No skeptic reason holds up: the field fails 1.3.5 for the reason the claim names.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the Password field of the same Sign in form (type="password", name loginPassword, posting to Account-Login), so it asks for the user's current password; its captured markup has no autocomplete attribute and the form sets none, so the claim is true of the capture. Reasons I weighed for a pass: current-password is explicitly in WCAG 2.1's Input Purposes list, so the field is in scope; type="password" alone does not say whether the password is current or new, and no script on the site adds autocomplete (I searched the base, main and secondary bundles; the snapshot is the post-script DOM). The tray being off-canvas until opened does not take it out of the page users receive. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same input without autocomplete (the register form's password nearby even has autocomplete="off"), so the capture does not differ. The field fails 1.3.5 as the claim says.
